_note: DD Form 1289 'DOD Prescription' - a US military compounding form, evidently a training/sample specimen (patient 'John R. Doe, HM3, USN' aboard 'U.S.S. Neverforgotten', signed Jack R. Frost, LCDR MD USNR, dated 23 Jan 99). Structured in classical prescription parts: Inscription (Tr. Belladonna 15 ml, Amphogel qs ad 120 ml), Subscription (M & Ft Solution = mix and make a solution), Signa (5ml TID a.c. = before meals). Both ingredients are recorded as medicines: unlike the cocoa-butter base in 25.jpg, Amphogel (aluminium hydroxide) is itself an active antacid even though it also makes up the volume. Split 'mixed' - the printed form furniture (MFGR, LOT NO, EXP DATE, Superscription/Inscription/Subscription/Signa labels) dominates the page and is exactly the kind of text that must not be read as drugs. raw_text omitted deliberately - the dense printed form labels make a faithful full transcription unreliable.
